text:
oliver: Hey — PR #8421 (request-splitter) is green and tests passed but I'm blocked on merge. Need a short architecture writeup + RFC URL attached to the PR before we can gate it. This changes routing so small requests take a fast-path; main risks are cache invalidation and shard affinity. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8421 cc @tara @ben

tara: Ack. Can you paste the RFC link and a one-liner summary here so I can skim quickly?

oliver: RFC draft: https://r.rw/rfc/request-splitter-v1 (internal). One-liner: route <256-token requests to a lightweight handler to cut p99 latency ~40% for short prompts. See "Safeguards" for kv-cache TTL and shard pinning notes.

ben: Quick q — what's the expected SLO delta and the rollback plan if cache miss rate spikes? :eyes:

natalie: I can author a 3-bullet arch narrative and attach it to the PR. Ben, can you confirm whether infra needs to follow up with metric dashboards or alerts?

ben: Infra follow-up: yes — add `fastpath.cache.miss_rate` and `fastpath.request_routing_errors`. Canary plan: 1% traffic for 2h, then 5% for 6h, then 25% if stable. I'll paste the metric checks into the PR description. No security review required — no customer data path changes.

natalie: I'll add the arch note and paste the RFC link under the PR's "Design" section. Rollback steps will be: set `ENABLE_FASTPATH=false` and flip routing back to stable pool. Example rollout/rollback commands below.

natalie: ```bash
# rollback to safe path
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-service ENABLE_FASTPATH=false
# internal toggle (ops only)
curl -X POST https://internal-ops/api/route-toggle -d '{"fastpath":false}'
```

arch-bot: automated: linked RFC https://r.rw/rfc/request-splitter-v1 to PR #8421 (metadata updated).

oliver: Thanks all — once the one-paragraph arch note and RFC link are attached I'll run the initial canary and merge. Planning to merge tomorrow 11:00 PT if no objections.

tara: +1

ben: LGTM, thanks.
